title: Joel And Kerri (Chas McIvor)
style: Afro-folk acoustic guitar mbira thumb piano warm baritone male vocal storytelling 104bpm brushed drums African rhythmic pulse Zimbabwe-Australia family portrait unhurried celebratory
lyrics:
[Intro - mbira and acoustic guitar, warm and unhurried]
Two worlds, one road
A farm in Zimbabwe, a life yet to be told

[Verse 1]
She grew up where the red dust rises
Where the msasa trees catch the morning gold
Her father Jeff walked the rows at sunrise
Her mother Jill knew the dairy cold
The workers came because they trusted his word
The cows came home when the bell was heard
And somewhere in that red-earth certainty
A girl grew up knowing who she'd be

[Verse 2]
He came from the south side of somewhere different
A little brother with a lot of heart
He didn't know a thing about Zimbabwe
But he knew enough to know this was the start
The family flew to a country wetter and cooler
Traded the veld for a southern sky
And somewhere in the crossing of those distances
He looked at her and didn't ask why

[Chorus]
Joel and Kerri
Red dust and southern rain
Joel and Kerri
Two homelands in one name
The mbira plays and the gum trees answer
From Harare to the harbour light
Joel and Kerri
Getting it exactly right

[Bridge - spoken, warm]
Jeff would approve. He was that kind of man.
Jill would be quietly pleased and say nothing for a moment.
Then she'd go put the kettle on.
Which is how you know it's serious.

[Chorus reprise]
Joel and Kerri
Red dust and southern rain
Joel and Kerri
Two homelands in one name

[Outro - mbira fading, acoustic guitar staying]
The farm is still there in the stories
Australia is there in the address
And somewhere between the two of them
They've made something worth more than either
Joel and Kerri
Yes
